statement.p: Calculate the derivative using the appropriate rule or combination of rules. f(x)=\frac{e^{x}}{\left(e^{x}+1\right)\mathopen{}\left(x+1\right)}

static.solution: f'(x) we begin with quotient rule f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+1)(x+1)\frac{d}{dx}[e^x]-e^x\frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+1)(x+1)]}{((e^x+1)(x+1))^2}. Next, recall that \frac{d}{dx}[e^x]=e^x, and use the product rule to compute \frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+1)(x+1)]=\frac{d}{dx}[e^x+1](x+1)+(e^x+1)\frac{d}{dx}[x+1] which is (e^x)(x+1)+(e^x+1)(1). Therefore f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+1)(x+1)\cdot e^x-e^x\cdot (e^x(x+1)+(e^x+1))}{((e^x+1)(x+1))^2} and after factoring out e^x in the numerator, expanding (e^x+1)(x+1)=xe^x+1\cdot e^x+1 x+1\cdot 1, and distributing the minus sign, we get f'(x)=\frac{e^x(xe^x+1 x+1 e^x - xe^x-1 e^x-e^x-1)}{((e^x+1)(x+1))^2} which simplifies to f'(x)=\frac{e^x(1 x - e^x-1)}{((e^x+1)(x+1))^2}.
